mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly different from zero during triggered periods at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces input demand and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 35% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically negative at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening and inflationary pressure regime, which increases both discount rates and cost pressures, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 10% for two consecutive months signals a housing market recovery, which boosts construction-related equities and supports broader market returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-mo moving average by > 10% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over a two-month period indicates a labor market normalization after a shock, which supports stable consumer demand and reduces uncertainty, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises AND UNRATE rises over 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive during triggered episodes at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in Real Personal Income (proxied by RSAFS) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals weakening household purchasing power, which reduces demand for goods and services and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes at 90% confidence.
